spread-list-1
# A LIST'S NON-ELEMENTS DO NOT CONSUME A PATH INDEX (BUGS.md 44).
# A `&:` spread constrains the elements and a `k:v` pair in list
# position is not one, so neither is an element and neither may take an
# index. Generation always agreed -- the array is built right in both
# ports -- but @tabnas/path's `@elem-ao` increments its index for every
# elem rule, so in TypeScript each non-element stole one and every LATER
# element's path came out one too high. `[&:integer,10,20,"bad"]` named
# `$.a.3` while `aontu get $.a.2` returned the offending value, and on a
# one-element list the path pointed past the end. Go was right
# throughout.
# These rows assert the PATH, not just the code. That is the point of
# them: both ports emitted `no_scalar_unify` all along, so a code-only
# row -- which is what nearly every error row in this suite is -- agreed
# in both engines while the paths disagreed. The path is the field
# `vet --format json` hands an agent.
# Every expectation below was obtained by running BOTH engines and
# diffing, per the parity probe.
spread-list-elem-path
spread-list-elem-path-code
spread-list-elem-path-single
spread-list-elem-path-mid
spread-list-elem-path-before
spread-list-pair-path
# Generation was never wrong; pinned so a future path fix cannot buy
# correct labels by changing what the array holds.
spread-list-gen-spread
spread-list-gen-pair
spread-list-gen-mid
# A PAIR BEFORE THE SPREAD DOES NOT CANCEL IT (BUGS.md 46).
# The `elem` rule marked all four of its alternatives `spread: true` --
# that flag is what says "contributes no element" -- and the SPREAD
# collector then took every one of them, so a `k:v` pair in list
# position was collected as if it were a `&:` spread. ListVal's
# `'&' === spread.o` test rejected the resulting entry and the real
# constraint went with it: `a:[x:1,&:integer,"bad"]` generated
# `{"a":["bad"]}` and exited 0 on the TypeScript side while Go refused.
# Order-dependence in a commutative language, and silent wrong output on
# the canonical port. `pair` now distinguishes the two.
spread-list-pair-before-spread
spread-list-pair-before-spread-path
spread-list-pairs-before-spread
spread-list-pairs-before-spread-path
# The commutativity itself: the same list with the pair AFTER the
# spread was already correct, and the two orders must stay one answer.
spread-list-pair-after-spread-path

spread-list-pair-before-spread-gen
